candidate.title: GMUCT 2.0
candidate.scope: Schematic-level architecture of the single assigned GMUCT 2.0 poster row, from the Degraded RNA input through poly(A) selection, RNA 5′-adapter ligation, adapter-bearing random-hexamer priming, reverse transcription and index PCR to indexed cDNA. The card identifies a single source row, and the matched secondary collection separately captions the 1.0 and 2.0 schematics. The neighboring upper GMUCT 1.0 row and clipped PARE text are context, not alternatives within this assigned workflow; no states, operations or flows from those rows are included. This resolves the previous scope expansion while retaining the supported five-operation 2.0 route. The yellow-highlighted uncapped poly(A) RNA identifies the biological target; Degraded RNA describes the input rather than an experimental degradation instruction. The key, reference footer and mobile-display QR graphic are annotations. The collection page is a verified secondary match under its GMUCT heading. Its prose-only additional poly(A) cleanup is not inserted into the drawn chain. Sequencing is an intended use of the cDNA library, not a depicted operation. GMUCT is expanded in the drawing as genome-wide mapping of uncapped transcripts and in the primary title as genome-wide mapping of uncapped and cleaved transcripts; these describe the same scoped method. Primary papers were inspected at metadata/abstract level only; detailed primer polarity is supported by the matched secondary catalogue. No full implementation equivalence, historical development edge or invention date is asserted.

evidence.locator: GMUCT 2.0: target RNA-adapter junction, adapter-bearing random primer, RT and indexed cDNA endpoint
evidence.rationale: The first ligation marks a pre-existing RNA 5′ boundary. Copying that junction into cDNA preserves its association with adjacent RNA sequence; random priming defines the opposite insert boundary. Only target-derived cDNAs with both adapter interfaces are represented in the continuing library class. The primary abstract lists several eligible biological origins, so this association does not by itself distinguish a decay or cleavage pathway or establish complete recovery.

states.label: Indexed cDNA
features: PCR-amplified indexed DNA library derived from the ligatable, poly(A)-selected uncapped/cleaved RNA subset; DNA is the sequencing carrier.

The original RNA-adapter junction associates adjacent RNA-derived sequence with a pre-existing uncapped 5′ end. The opposite insert boundary is set by random priming, not necessarily by a biological cleavage.
The depicted index labels the sequencing library; no cell barcode or unique molecular identifier is specified.

Eligible RNA can arise from decapping/decay or small-RNA-directed cleavage, as reported in the primary abstract. Capture of an end alone does not identify its pathway of origin or establish recovery of every uncapped RNA.

method_scopes.rationale: All five local operations are in the lower row explicitly assigned to GMUCT 2.0. The single-row card and separately captioned secondary schematic establish this scope. GMUCT 1.0 is a neighboring independent entry, so its oligo-dT priming, PCR/fragmentation and downstream adapter-ligation route are excluded rather than reassigned to 2.0. Starting RNA selection and ligation retain their local input history through random priming and RT. The Willmann abstract establishes the named 2.0 protocol and ligatable-end principle; the diagram and secondary catalogue support detailed schematic interfaces. The prose-only additional poly(A) cleanup is outside the depicted chain. Applicability is resolved at schematic scope, without asserting a complete primary-methods reconstruction.
